title: Validate Signup
summary: Check a signup form and return it as a `signup`, with `age` as a number. The username must be 3 to 16 characters (`username: must be 3 to 16 characters`), the email must have exactly one `@` with text on both sides (`email: must look like name@host`), and the age must be only ASCII digits (`age: not a number`) and at least 13 (`age: must be at least 13`). If anything is wrong, fail once with every problem, in that order, so the user can fix them all in one go. Each field reports at most one problem.
hints: Don't return at the first problem. Check every field, add each problem to a list, and fail at the end if the list isn't empty.

Put every problem in the error's message, for example joined with `; `. Python's `ExceptionGroup` and JavaScript's `AggregateError` keep the parts beside the message, not in it: `str(ExceptionGroup("invalid", errs))` is `invalid (2 sub-exceptions)`. Go's `errors.Join` does include them. QML has no `AggregateError`.
Check the age's characters before converting: `-1` and `+20` aren't numbers in this form. Ages have at most 3 digits here.

cases.description: validate_signup accepts the shortest values allowed
validate_signup rejects an email without a name
validate_signup rejects an age that isn't a number
